Battle_of_Marathon.title: Battle of Marathon
Battle_of_Marathon.text: Athenian and Plataean hoplites defeat the first Persian invasion of Greece, a founding moment in Athenian self-confidence.

Battle_of_Salamis.title: Battle of Salamis
Battle_of_Salamis.text: The allied Greek fleet destroys much of Xerxes' navy in the narrows off Salamis, turning back the second Persian invasion.

Peloponnesian_War.title: Peloponnesian War begins
Peloponnesian_War.text: A 27-year war between the Athenian and Spartan alliances exhausts classical Greece and ends with Athens' defeat in 404 BCE.

Battle_of_Gaugamela.title: Battle of Gaugamela
Battle_of_Gaugamela.text: Alexander the Great defeats Darius III, bringing down the Achaemenid Persian Empire and opening the Hellenistic age.

Death_of_Alexander_the_Great.title: Death of Alexander
Death_of_Alexander_the_Great.text: Alexander dies in Babylon aged 32; his generals (the Diadochi) carve his empire into rival Hellenistic kingdoms.

Hannibal%27s_crossing_of_the_Alps.title: Hannibal crosses the Alps
Hannibal%27s_crossing_of_the_Alps.text: In the Second Punic War, Carthage's Hannibal marches an army with war elephants over the Alps to invade Roman Italy.

Siege_of_Carthage_(Third_Punic_War).title: Destruction of Carthage
Siege_of_Carthage_(Third_Punic_War).text: Rome razes Carthage at the end of the Third Punic War (and sacks Corinth the same year), becoming master of the Mediterranean.

Assassination_of_Julius_Caesar.title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
Assassination_of_Julius_Caesar.text: Senators stab the dictator Caesar on the Ides of March; the civil wars that follow end the Roman Republic.

Battle_of_Actium.title: Battle of Actium
Battle_of_Actium.text: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at sea; as Augustus he becomes the first Roman emperor in 27 BCE.

Battle_of_the_Teutoburg_Forest.title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
Battle_of_the_Teutoburg_Forest.text: Germanic tribes under Arminius destroy three Roman legions, halting Roman expansion east of the Rhine.

Hadrian%27s_Wall.title: Hadrian's Wall begun
Hadrian%27s_Wall.text: Emperor Hadrian orders a fortified wall across Britain, marking the empire's turn from expansion to defended frontiers.

Edict_of_Milan.title: Edict of Milan
Edict_of_Milan.text: Constantine and Licinius grant religious toleration across the empire, ending the persecution of Christians.

Constantinople.title: Constantinople founded
Constantinople.text: Constantine dedicates his new capital on the Bosporus; it will be the seat of the Eastern Roman Empire for over a thousand years.

Sack_of_Rome_(410).title: Sack of Rome
Sack_of_Rome_(410).text: Visigoths under Alaric sack Rome, the first time in 800 years the city has fallen to a foreign enemy.

Battle_of_the_Catalaunian_Plains.title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
Battle_of_the_Catalaunian_Plains.text: A Roman–Visigothic coalition under Aetius checks Attila's Huns in one of late antiquity's largest battles.

Fall_of_the_Western_Roman_Empire.title: End of the Western Roman Empire
Fall_of_the_Western_Roman_Empire.text: Odoacer deposes the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus; the date conventionally marks the end of Roman rule in the West.

Plague_of_Justinian.title: Plague of Justinian
Plague_of_Justinian.text: The first known pandemic of bubonic plague strikes the Mediterranean, killing a large share of the population of Constantinople.

Hijrah.title: The Hijra
Hijrah.text: Muhammad and his followers migrate from Mecca to Medina; the year becomes the start of the Islamic calendar.

Battle_of_the_Yarmuk.title: Battle of the Yarmuk
Battle_of_the_Yarmuk.text: Arab Muslim forces defeat the Byzantine army, opening Syria and the Levant to the early caliphate.

Umayyad_conquest_of_Hispania.title: Umayyad conquest of Hispania
Umayyad_conquest_of_Hispania.text: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses from North Africa and defeats the Visigothic king Roderic, beginning nearly eight centuries of al-Andalus.

Battle_of_Tours.title: Battle of Tours
Battle_of_Tours.text: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeat an Umayyad raiding army, strengthening Carolingian power in Gaul.

Charlemagne.title: Charlemagne crowned Emperor
Charlemagne.text: Pope Leo III crowns the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor on Christmas Day, reviving the imperial title in the West.

Treaty_of_Verdun.title: Treaty of Verdun
Treaty_of_Verdun.text: Charlemagne's grandsons divide the Carolingian Empire into three kingdoms, foreshadowing France and Germany.

Rurik.title: Rurik at Novgorod
Rurik.text: According to the Primary Chronicle, the Varangian Rurik is invited to rule Novgorod, the traditional beginning of the Rus' state.

Otto_the_Great.title: Otto I crowned Emperor
Otto_the_Great.text: The German king Otto I is crowned emperor, conventionally the founding of the Holy Roman Empire.

Christianization_of_Kievan_Rus%27.title: Christianization of Kievan Rus'
Christianization_of_Kievan_Rus%27.text: Grand Prince Vladimir adopts Byzantine Orthodox Christianity, shaping the religious culture of Eastern Europe.

East%E2%80%93West_Schism.title: East–West Schism
East%E2%80%93West_Schism.text: Mutual excommunications between papal legates and the Patriarch of Constantinople formalize the split of Catholic and Orthodox churches.

Battle_of_Hastings.title: Battle of Hastings
Battle_of_Hastings.text: William of Normandy defeats Harold II, beginning the Norman conquest of England.

Battle_of_Manzikert.title: Battle of Manzikert
Battle_of_Manzikert.text: The Seljuk Turks defeat and capture the Byzantine emperor, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

Siege_of_Jerusalem_(1099).title: Crusaders take Jerusalem
Siege_of_Jerusalem_(1099).text: The First Crusade captures Jerusalem after a siege and massacre, founding the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem.

Sack_of_Constantinople.title: Sack of Constantinople
Sack_of_Constantinople.text: The Fourth Crusade turns on Constantinople and sacks it, gravely weakening the Byzantine Empire.

Magna_Carta.title: Magna Carta
Magna_Carta.text: Rebel barons force King John to seal a charter limiting royal power, later a touchstone of constitutional government.

Siege_of_Kiev_(1240).title: Mongols sack Kyiv
Siege_of_Kiev_(1240).text: Batu Khan's Mongol army destroys Kyiv during the invasion of Rus', beginning the era of the Golden Horde.

Siege_of_Baghdad_(1258).title: Mongols sack Baghdad
Siege_of_Baghdad_(1258).text: Hulegu's army takes Baghdad and kills the caliph, ending the Abbasid Caliphate's rule from the city.

Black_Death.title: Black Death reaches Europe
Black_Death.text: Plague arrives on Genoese ships from the Black Sea; within five years it kills perhaps a third or more of Europe's people.

Fall_of_Constantinople.title: Fall of Constantinople
Fall_of_Constantinople.text: Sultan Mehmed II captures the city, ending the Byzantine Empire; it becomes the Ottoman capital.

Fall_of_Granada.title: Fall of Granada
Fall_of_Granada.text: Castile and Aragon take the last Muslim state in Iberia; the same year Columbus sails west under the Spanish crown.

Ninety-five_Theses.title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
Ninety-five_Theses.text: Martin Luther challenges the sale of indulgences, sparking the Protestant Reformation.

Siege_of_Vienna_(1529).title: First Siege of Vienna
Siege_of_Vienna_(1529).text: Suleiman the Magnificent's Ottoman army besieges Vienna but withdraws, marking the limit of Ottoman advance in central Europe for a century.

Battle_of_Lepanto.title: Battle of Lepanto
Battle_of_Lepanto.text: The Holy League's galleys defeat the Ottoman fleet in the largest naval battle of the age of oared warships.

Spanish_Armada.title: Spanish Armada
Spanish_Armada.text: Philip II's invasion fleet is beaten off Gravelines and scattered by storms, securing Elizabethan England.

Thirty_Years%27_War.title: Thirty Years' War begins
Thirty_Years%27_War.text: The Defenestration of Prague triggers a war that devastates the German lands and draws in most of Europe.

Peace_of_Westphalia.title: Peace of Westphalia
Peace_of_Westphalia.text: Treaties end the Thirty Years' War and the Eighty Years' War, often cited as the origin of the modern system of sovereign states.

Battle_of_Vienna.title: Battle of Vienna
Battle_of_Vienna.text: A relief army led by Jan III Sobieski breaks the Ottoman siege, beginning the Habsburg reconquest of Hungary.

Saint_Petersburg.title: Saint Petersburg founded
Saint_Petersburg.text: Peter the Great founds a new capital on the Baltic as Russia's "window to Europe".

French_Revolution.title: French Revolution
French_Revolution.text: The storming of the Bastille on 14 July becomes the symbol of a revolution that overturns the old regime in France.

Battle_of_Austerlitz.title: Battle of Austerlitz
Battle_of_Austerlitz.text: Napoleon defeats Russia and Austria; the Holy Roman Empire is dissolved the following year.

French_invasion_of_Russia.title: Napoleon's invasion of Russia
French_invasion_of_Russia.text: The Grande Armée reaches a burning Moscow but is destroyed in the winter retreat, breaking Napoleon's power.

Congress_of_Vienna.title: Waterloo and the Congress of Vienna
Congress_of_Vienna.text: Napoleon's final defeat at Waterloo coincides with the Vienna settlement that redraws Europe's map for a generation.

Revolutions_of_1848.title: Revolutions of 1848
Revolutions_of_1848.text: A wave of liberal and national uprisings spreads across Europe; most are suppressed, but serfdom ends in Austria.

Suez_Canal.title: Suez Canal opens
Suez_Canal.text: The canal links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, transforming trade between Europe and Asia.

Proclamation_of_the_German_Empire.title: German Empire proclaimed
Proclamation_of_the_German_Empire.text: After victory over France, Wilhelm I is proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors, completing German unification.

Congress_of_Berlin.title: Congress of Berlin
Congress_of_Berlin.text: The great powers revise the Balkan settlement after the Russo-Turkish War; Romania, Serbia and Montenegro become independent.

Assassination_of_Archduke_Franz_Ferdinan.title: Assassination in Sarajevo
Assassination_of_Archduke_Franz_Ferdinan.text: The killing of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sets off the July Crisis and the First World War.

Battle_of_Verdun.title: Battle of Verdun
Battle_of_Verdun.text: A ten-month battle of attrition between France and Germany becomes a symbol of the Western Front.

Russian_Revolution.title: Russian Revolution
Russian_Revolution.text: The tsar abdicates in February and the Bolsheviks seize power in October, leading to the Soviet state.

Treaty_of_Versailles.title: Treaty of Versailles
Treaty_of_Versailles.text: The peace settlement with Germany, alongside other Paris treaties, dismantles empires and creates new states across Central Europe.

Proclamation_of_the_Republic_of_Turkey.title: Republic of Turkey proclaimed
Proclamation_of_the_Republic_of_Turkey.text: After the Ottoman Empire's collapse, Mustafa Kemal proclaims the Turkish Republic with its capital at Ankara.

Invasion_of_Poland.title: Second World War begins
Invasion_of_Poland.text: Germany invades Poland on 1 September; Britain and France declare war two days later.

Battle_of_Stalingrad.title: Battle of Stalingrad
Battle_of_Stalingrad.text: The Soviet encirclement and destruction of the German Sixth Army marks a turning point of the war in Europe.

Normandy_landings.title: D-Day landings
Normandy_landings.text: Allied forces land in Normandy on 6 June, opening a western front against Nazi Germany.

Victory_in_Europe_Day.title: End of the war in Europe
Victory_in_Europe_Day.text: Berlin falls and Germany surrenders unconditionally in May; Europe is divided into occupation zones.

Treaty_of_Rome.title: Treaty of Rome
Treaty_of_Rome.text: Six countries found the European Economic Community, forerunner of the European Union.

Berlin_Wall.title: Berlin Wall built
Berlin_Wall.text: East Germany seals off West Berlin overnight, making the wall the emblem of the Cold War division.

Fall_of_the_Berlin_Wall.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
Fall_of_the_Berlin_Wall.text: Border crossings open on 9 November amid peaceful revolutions across Eastern Europe; Germany reunifies in 1990.

Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union.text: The USSR breaks into fifteen independent states, redrawing the map of Eastern Europe and the Caucasus.

Maastricht_Treaty.title: European Union founded
Maastricht_Treaty.text: The Maastricht Treaty takes effect, creating the EU and laying the groundwork for the euro.

2004_enlargement_of_the_European_Union.title: EU eastern enlargement
2004_enlargement_of_the_European_Union.text: Ten countries, most formerly in the Soviet sphere, join the European Union in its largest single expansion.

German_invasion_of_Belgium_(1914).title: German invasion of Belgium
German_invasion_of_Belgium_(1914).text: Germany invades neutral Belgium to outflank France under the Schlieffen Plan, bringing Britain into the war.

Battle_of_Tannenberg.title: Battle of Tannenberg
Battle_of_Tannenberg.text: German forces encircle and destroy the Russian Second Army in East Prussia within the first month of the war.

First_Battle_of_the_Marne.title: First Battle of the Marne
First_Battle_of_the_Marne.text: French and British counter-attacks halt the German advance on Paris; both sides then dig the trenches of the Western Front.

First_Battle_of_Ypres.title: First Battle of Ypres
First_Battle_of_Ypres.text: The 'race to the sea' ends in Flanders; the front line now runs unbroken from the Channel to Switzerland.

Armenian_genocide.title: Armenian genocide
Armenian_genocide.text: Ottoman authorities arrest Armenian leaders in Constantinople and begin mass deportations and killings; about a million Armenians die.

Gallipoli_campaign.title: Gallipoli landings
Gallipoli_campaign.text: Allied troops land on the Gallipoli peninsula to open the Dardanelles; the campaign fails and is abandoned in January 1916.

Battles_of_the_Isonzo.title: Battles of the Isonzo
Battles_of_the_Isonzo.text: After Italy joins the Allies, it launches the first of twelve costly offensives against Austria-Hungary along the Isonzo.

Battle_of_Jutland.title: Battle of Jutland
Battle_of_Jutland.text: The largest naval battle of the war; the German fleet inflicts heavier losses but never again challenges British control of the North Sea.

Brusilov_offensive.title: Brusilov offensive
Brusilov_offensive.text: Russia's most successful offensive of the war shatters much of the Austro-Hungarian army on the Eastern Front.

Arab_Revolt.title: Arab Revolt
Arab_Revolt.text: Sharif Hussein of Mecca rises against Ottoman rule with British support, opening a new front in Arabia and the Levant.

Battle_of_the_Somme.title: Battle of the Somme
Battle_of_the_Somme.text: A British and French offensive whose first day is the bloodiest in British military history; over a million men are killed or wounded.

Battle_of_Passchendaele.title: Battle of Passchendaele
Battle_of_Passchendaele.text: A British offensive in Flanders bogs down in rain and mud, gaining a few miles at enormous cost.

Battle_of_Caporetto.title: Battle of Caporetto
Battle_of_Caporetto.text: Austro-German forces break through the Italian line and drive it back to the Piave river.

Battle_of_Jerusalem.title: Capture of Jerusalem
Battle_of_Jerusalem.text: British forces under Allenby take Jerusalem from the Ottoman Empire during the Sinai and Palestine campaign.

Treaty_of_Brest-Litovsk.title: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
Treaty_of_Brest-Litovsk.text: Soviet Russia leaves the war, ceding the Baltic lands, Poland, Belarus and Ukraine to German control.

German_spring_offensive.title: German spring offensive
German_spring_offensive.text: Germany's last great offensive gains ground quickly but exhausts its army before American troops arrive in strength.

Hundred_Days_Offensive.title: Hundred Days Offensive
Hundred_Days_Offensive.text: Beginning at Amiens, Allied attacks push the German army back across the Western Front in a war of movement.

Armistice_of_11_November_1918.title: Armistice of 11 November
Armistice_of_11_November_1918.text: Germany signs an armistice in a railway carriage at Compiègne; fighting on the Western Front ends at 11 a.m.

Anschluss.title: Anschluss
Anschluss.text: Nazi Germany annexes Austria, the first of Hitler's territorial expansions without war.

Munich_Agreement.title: Munich Agreement
Munich_Agreement.text: Britain, France and Italy allow Germany to annex the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia, the high point of appeasement.

Molotov%E2%80%93Ribbentrop_Pact.title: Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
Molotov%E2%80%93Ribbentrop_Pact.text: Germany and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression pact with a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe between them.

Winter_War.title: Winter War
Winter_War.text: The Soviet Union invades Finland; Finland resists for over three months before ceding territory.

Operation_Weser%C3%BCbung.title: Invasion of Denmark and Norway
Operation_Weser%C3%BCbung.text: Germany occupies Denmark in a day and invades Norway to secure Swedish iron ore and North Atlantic bases.

Battle_of_France.title: Battle of France
Battle_of_France.text: German armour breaks through the Ardennes; the Netherlands, Belgium and France fall within six weeks.

Dunkirk_evacuation.title: Dunkirk evacuation
Dunkirk_evacuation.text: More than 330,000 British and French soldiers are evacuated by sea from the beaches of Dunkirk.

Battle_of_Britain.title: Battle of Britain
Battle_of_Britain.text: The Royal Air Force defeats the Luftwaffe's attempt to win air superiority over Britain, ending invasion plans.

Invasion_of_Yugoslavia.title: Invasion of Yugoslavia and Greece
Invasion_of_Yugoslavia.text: Axis forces overrun Yugoslavia and Greece in a few weeks, securing the Balkans before the attack on the Soviet Union.

Battle_of_Crete.title: Battle of Crete
Battle_of_Crete.text: German paratroopers seize Crete in the first large airborne invasion in history, at heavy cost.

Operation_Barbarossa.title: Operation Barbarossa
Operation_Barbarossa.text: Germany and its allies invade the Soviet Union along a front from the Baltic to the Black Sea, the largest invasion in history.

Siege_of_Leningrad.title: Siege of Leningrad
Siege_of_Leningrad.text: German and Finnish forces cut off Leningrad; the 872-day siege kills around a million civilians, mostly by starvation.

Battle_of_Moscow.title: Battle of Moscow
Battle_of_Moscow.text: The German drive on Moscow is stopped at the city's approaches, and a Soviet winter counter-offensive pushes it back.

Wannsee_Conference.title: Wannsee Conference
Wannsee_Conference.text: Senior Nazi officials coordinate the 'Final Solution', the systematic murder of Europe's Jews in the Holocaust.

Second_Battle_of_El_Alamein.title: Second Battle of El Alamein
Second_Battle_of_El_Alamein.text: British Commonwealth forces defeat Rommel's Axis army in Egypt, turning the tide in North Africa.

Battle_of_Kursk.title: Battle of Kursk
Battle_of_Kursk.text: Germany's last major offensive in the East fails; the Red Army takes the strategic initiative for the rest of the war.

Allied_invasion_of_Sicily.title: Allied invasion of Sicily
Allied_invasion_of_Sicily.text: Allied landings in Sicily lead to Mussolini's fall and Italy's armistice in September.

Operation_Bagration.title: Operation Bagration
Operation_Bagration.text: A massive Soviet offensive destroys German Army Group Centre and advances to the Vistula.

Warsaw_Uprising.title: Warsaw Uprising
Warsaw_Uprising.text: The Polish Home Army rises against German occupation; after 63 days the uprising is crushed and the city razed.

Battle_of_the_Bulge.title: Battle of the Bulge
Battle_of_the_Bulge.text: Germany's last offensive in the West surprises the Allies in the Ardennes but is defeated within weeks.

Auschwitz_concentration_camp.title: Liberation of Auschwitz
Auschwitz_concentration_camp.text: Soviet troops liberate Auschwitz-Birkenau, where about 1.1 million people, most of them Jews, were murdered.

Yalta_Conference.title: Yalta Conference
Yalta_Conference.text: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin plan Germany's defeat and occupation and the post-war order in Europe.

Potsdam_Conference.title: Potsdam Conference
Potsdam_Conference.text: The victorious Allies settle Germany's occupation zones, the new Polish border and the expulsion of Germans from the East.

phases.ww1_1914: End of 1914: the Western Front digs in
phases.ww1_1915: End of 1915: Russian Poland and Serbia occupied
phases.ww1_1917: End of 1917: Caporetto; Baghdad and Jerusalem fall
phases.ww1_1918: July 1918: Brest-Litovsk and the spring offensives
phases.ww2_1941: December 1941: at the gates of Moscow
phases.ww2_1943: End of 1943: Soviet advance, Italy divided
